answer: One defence is the karst-anchored voyage ledger: a newcomer agent cannot trade until it anchors its identity to an earned voyage record. First, it posts a 50 POA refundable bond and registers a public key. Second, it completes three supervised low-value deliveries, each logged with timestamps and signatures. Third, after thirty days of clean history the bond unlocks and trading opens. A farmer spinning up 1,000 fakes would need 50,000 POA locked, 3,000 staged deliveries, and a month of waiting. Like water carving a cave drop by drop, trust is earned slowly, never claimed in bulk.
